archetype.name: Bubble Team (power-play reliant)
archetype.definition: A team whose winning record rests on an elite power play, decent goaltending and close-game breaks, while it is outshot and out-chanced at 5-on-5, which is the profile of a club fighting for a wild-card spot rather than one that controls games.

report.headline: A 103-point pace built on the power play, not on 5-on-5 play
report.take:
Winnipeg is eight games into a bounce-back attempt after a 2025-26 that finished with 82 points and 26th on the site. That came one year after the 116-point, first-ranked 2024-25 team. The 4-2-2 start and a 103-point pace look like a return toward that peak. The underlying play looks much more like last year. The Jets have been outscored on the season (23 goals for, 24 against). They rank 26th in 5-on-5 expected-goal share at 46.7% and 22nd in shot attempts at 47%, and they allow 29.1 shots a game, 25th in the league and well above the league's 26.3.

What keeps the record afloat is special teams and one line. The power play is converting 30%, third in the league and nearly ten points above average. That is close to the 28.9% unit of the 2024-25 juggernaut and far from last year's 18.5%. Kyle Connor has 8 goals and 11 points and sits third on the left-wing tab. Cole Perfetti, fifth among centers, adds 5 goals, and both have 5 power-play points. Below them the forward group thins quickly, which is why it grades D+: Gabriel Vilardi has no goals in nearly 17 minutes a night, and Viggo Björck has no points and is 201st of 220 centers.

The numbers flatter the Jets in two ways. Points vs Goal Diff is +1.4, fifth in the league: a minus-one team has banked points through narrow 3-2 wins over Detroit, Pittsburgh and Colorado and two overtime losses. Goaltending has also been above average, with Stuart Skinner at +2.7 GSAx in his five starts. That is good, but it is nowhere near the 40-plus seasons this franchise had at its best, so it cannot cover heavy shot volume for long. The goals-differential pace of minus-10 is a truer read of this team than the points pace.

The direction depends on whether the 5-on-5 game catches up to the special teams. The last five games went 2-2-1 at a .500 points rate, and the Jets allowed more than their season average over that stretch. If the power play cools toward the league's 20.4%, the record will drift toward the middle of the Central.

strengths.title: An elite, top-heavy power play
strengths.body: At 30% the power play ranks third and runs well above the league average, and it is the main reason the offense is not worse than 22nd in scoring. Connor and Perfetti each have 5 power-play points, so the unit has two real finishers. The 2024-25 team sustained a similar rate, so some of this is real. Thirty percent over eight games will still come down.

strengths.title: Connor and Perfetti carrying the scoring
strengths.body: Connor's 8 goals on 37 shots make him one of the league's most dangerous wingers so far, ranked third on his tab. Perfetti ranks fifth among 220 centers, and both post on-ice expected-goal shares above 50% while the team sits well below it. Their talent is sustainable. Connor's finishing rate is not, and there is little scoring behind them to absorb a cold week.

strengths.title: Skinner giving above-average saves
strengths.body: The goalies are +2.4 GSAx as a group, 12th in the league, with a B grade. Skinner has done the work at +2.7 and a .906 save %, while Clay Stevenson has been slightly below expected in three starts. Against the shot volume this team allows, Skinner holding this level is a requirement, not a bonus.

concerns.title: Losing the 5-on-5 battle
concerns.body: An xGF % of 46.7% ranks 26th, and the Jets give up 29.1 shots a game, among the most in the league. This is not one bad night: they were also under 50% in expected-goal share last season. Unless it improves, the goaltending and the power play have to cover a structural deficit every night.

concerns.title: Record running ahead of the margin
concerns.body: The Jets have 10 standings points despite a negative goal differential, and their Pts vs Goal Diff of +1.4 is fifth in the league. Most of the wins have come by a single goal, and close-game results tend to even out. The minus-10 differential pace is the more honest projection of where this goes.

concerns.title: No scoring depth behind the top
concerns.body: The forward group grades D+ because the middle-six has gone dry. Vilardi has no goals while playing nearly 17 minutes, Morgan Barron has none either, and Björck has no points with a -4. When the power play has an off night, there is no secondary source of offense.

trend.note: The start went three straight one-goal wins, a 5-1 loss to Anaheim, a win over Minnesota, then two overtime losses and a regulation loss. The last five games ran 2-2-1 at a .500 points rate, slightly below the season rate, with more goals allowed. The Jets are treading water rather than building.

weekAhead.headline: Two leaky goaltending teams, then Dallas's wall and Florida's possession
weekAhead.body:
The week splits in two. The road trip opens in St. Louis, which is the friendliest matchup on paper: the Blues have a .877 save % and a C- goaltending grade, and they have allowed the most production to centers in the league. That suits Perfetti and Scheifele. Dallas is the opposite problem. The Stars rank first in goals against, have a .944 save %, carry +9.6 GSAx and have held forwards furthest under expectation of any team. Their own offense is 27th, though, so expect a low-scoring game that the Jets' goaltending can keep close.

Back home, Montréal out-chances opponents at 54.3% but stops little, with a .868 save % that ranks 28th and a defense that ranks 29th at containing wingers. That is an opening for Connor. Florida is the test: sixth on the site, 58% shot attempts, B+ grades across the board. The Panthers are exactly the kind of possession team that exposes Winnipeg's 5-on-5 numbers. Two points out of the Montréal and St. Louis games each looks likely. Dallas and Florida look like games the Jets will have to steal.

keyMatchups.title: Jets centers against St. Louis
keyMatchups.body: St. Louis ranks last in points allowed to centers relative to expectation, and nearly half the points against it come from the middle. Perfetti and Scheifele are the beneficiaries, and a Blues goaltending group at .877 makes it a good night to bank goals before the harder half of the week.

keyMatchups.title: The power play against Dallas
keyMatchups.body: Dallas kills 89.3% of penalties, fourth in the league, behind a goalie group running a .944 save %. Winnipeg's 30% power play is its best weapon, and this is where it is least likely to work. If the Jets cannot score on the man advantage here, their 5-on-5 game probably cannot win the night.

keyMatchups.title: Florida's possession versus Winnipeg's shot volume
keyMatchups.body: Florida takes 58% of 5-on-5 shot attempts, third in the league, while Winnipeg sits 22nd. The game will likely be played in the Jets' end. Skinner's form will decide whether it stays close.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Winnipeg can win any 5-on-5 shot battle, especially against Montréal and Florida, or keeps needing the power play and Skinner to bail it out.

restOfSeason.body:
The likeliest path is a team that hovers around .500 on goal differential and lands in the Central's wild-card scrum. The points pace of 103 will not hold, because it is built on a top-five Pts vs Goal Diff and a power play at a level few teams sustain. Expect the record to sag toward the low 90s in standings points. Connor, Perfetti and a competent Skinner keep it from collapsing to last year's 82.

What would change that forecast is the 5-on-5 game. This roster produced a 52.9% expected-goal share during its 116-point season, and its current 46.7% is closer to last year's slide. A real improvement there, or a scorer emerging from the middle-six, makes this a solid playoff team. Without one, the Jets are a bubble team whose fate depends on the power play and the goaltending.
swingFactors: How far the power play regresses from 30%
Skinner sustaining above-expected goaltending against heavy volume
Secondary scoring from Vilardi and the middle-six

confidence.note: Only eight games, but the 5-on-5 deficit matches last season's profile.
